name: Mercury
day: 58.6 Earth days (sidereal); a solar day lasts 176 Earth days
summary: The smallest planet and closest to the Sun, a cratered iron-rich world with almost no atmosphere.
surface: Heavily cratered like the Moon, with huge cliffs (lobate scarps) formed as the planet cooled and shrank; ice hides in permanently shadowed polar craters.
atmosphere: An ultra-thin exosphere of sodium, potassium and oxygen blasted off the surface by solar wind.
interior: An enormous iron core makes up ~85% of its radius; it has a weak global magnetic field.
exploration: Mariner 10 (1974–75), MESSENGER (orbited 2011–15) and BepiColombo (ESA–JAXA), which entered orbit around Mercury on 21 November 2026.
facts_list: Biggest day–night temperature swing of any planet
Its year is shorter than two of its solar days

name: Venus
summary: Earth's 'twin' in size, with a runaway greenhouse that makes it the hottest planet.
surface: Volcanic plains, pancake domes and highland 'continents' (Ishtar, Aphrodite); possibly active volcanoes today (Maat Mons changes seen in Magellan data).
atmosphere: Crushing CO₂ atmosphere 92 times Earth's surface pressure, with sulfuric-acid clouds and winds that circle the planet in 4 days (super-rotation).
interior: Rocky with an iron core, but no measurable magnetic field.
exploration: Venera landers (USSR) returned the first images from another planet's surface (1975); Magellan radar-mapped it; future missions DAVINCI, VERITAS and EnVision.
facts_list: Spins backwards
A day is longer than its year
Phosphine detection (2020) is disputed

name: Earth
summary: The only known world with life, liquid surface oceans and active plate tectonics.
surface: 71% ocean; plate tectonics recycles the crust and regulates climate over millions of years.
atmosphere: 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen; ozone layer shields UV; strong magnetic field deflects solar wind.
interior: Iron-nickel core generates the geodynamo; mantle convection drives plates.
exploration: Observed by thousands of satellites; humans have lived continuously in orbit since 2000 (ISS).
facts_list: Densest planet
Only planet not named after a god

name: Mars
summary: A cold desert world with the largest volcano and canyon in the solar system and a watery past.
surface: Olympus Mons (~22 km high), Valles Marineris (~4,000 km long), ancient river deltas such as Jezero, polar ice caps of water and CO₂.
atmosphere: Thin CO₂ atmosphere (<1% of Earth's pressure); global dust storms.
interior: Lost its global magnetic field ~4 billion years ago; InSight measured a liquid iron core and marsquakes.
exploration: Viking (1976), Spirit and Opportunity, Curiosity, Perseverance with Ingenuity helicopter, China's Zhurong, India's Mangalyaan (2014, first Asian Mars orbiter, first-attempt success).
facts_list: Perseverance found a 'potential biosignature' at Sapphire Canyon (2025)
Mars Sample Return was cancelled in 2026

name: Jupiter
summary: The giant of the solar system, more than twice as massive as all other planets combined.
surface: No solid surface; colourful belts and zones; the Great Red Spot is a storm larger than Earth that has raged for at least 190 years.
atmosphere: Hydrogen and helium with ammonia clouds; lightning and auroras.
interior: Metallic hydrogen layer creates the strongest planetary magnetic field; Juno found a 'fuzzy', dilute core.
exploration: Pioneer, Voyager, Galileo (1995–2003), Juno (since 2016), ESA's JUICE (arrives 2031), Europa Clipper (arrives 2030).
facts_list: Shortest day of any planet
Its magnetosphere is the largest structure in the solar system

name: Saturn
summary: The ringed planet, so low in density it would float in a big enough bathtub.
surface: Gaseous; a hexagonal jet stream at its north pole.
atmosphere: Hydrogen and helium; winds up to 1,800 km/h.
interior: Rocky-icy core within metallic hydrogen; rings made of mostly water ice, possibly only a few hundred million years old.
exploration: Pioneer 11, Voyagers, Cassini–Huygens (2004–2017, ended by diving into Saturn); Dragonfly to Titan launches ~2028.
facts_list: Has the most known moons
Rings are ~280,000 km wide but often only ~10 m thick

name: Uranus
summary: An ice giant tipped on its side, rolling around the Sun with extreme seasons.
atmosphere: Hydrogen, helium, methane; coldest planetary atmosphere measured (−224°C).
interior: Water, ammonia and methane 'ices' around a rocky core; offset, tilted magnetic field.
exploration: Only Voyager 2 (1986) has visited; a Uranus Orbiter and Probe is the top US flagship priority.
facts_list: Axial tilt ~98°
Each pole gets 42 years of sunlight then 42 of darkness

name: Neptune
summary: The most distant planet, found by mathematics before it was seen.
surface: Deep blue; Great Dark Spot storms that come and go.
atmosphere: Fastest winds in the solar system, ~2,100 km/h.
interior: Ice giant like Uranus; emits more heat than it gets from the Sun.
exploration: Predicted by Le Verrier and Adams, observed by Galle in 1846; only Voyager 2 visited (1989).
facts_list: Has completed only one orbit since its discovery (2011)
Moon Triton orbits backwards

name: Pluto
summary: The best-known dwarf planet, with nitrogen glaciers and a heart-shaped plain.
surface: Sputnik Planitia, a nitrogen-ice glacier basin; water-ice mountains up to 3.5 km; possible subsurface ocean.
atmosphere: Thin nitrogen atmosphere with blue haze layers.
interior: Rocky core with an icy mantle.
exploration: Discovered by Clyde Tombaugh in 1930; reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006; New Horizons flew by in 2015.
facts_list: Charon is so large they orbit a point between them
Its orbit crosses Neptune's

name: Ceres
summary: The largest object in the asteroid belt and the only dwarf planet in the inner solar system.
surface: Bright salt deposits (sodium carbonate) in Occator crater from briny water below.
interior: Rock and ice, with a possible brine reservoir.
exploration: Discovered by Piazzi in 1801; Dawn orbited it 2015–18.
facts_list: First asteroid discovered
Holds about a third of the asteroid belt's mass

name: Eris
summary: A distant dwarf planet nearly Pluto's size whose discovery led to Pluto's reclassification.
atmosphere: Possibly a collapsed atmosphere frozen onto the surface.
exploration: Discovered in 2005 by Brown, Trujillo and Rabinowitz.
facts_list: More massive than Pluto

name: Haumea
summary: An egg-shaped dwarf planet spinning every 4 hours, with a ring.
facts_list: Fastest-spinning large body known in the solar system

name: Makemake
summary: A reddish Kuiper Belt dwarf planet named after a Rapa Nui creator god.
facts_list: Its moon (MK2) was found in 2016
